template.title: Sample Diagnosis Name
template.summary: A short, plain-language explanation of what the result means.
actions: Give one low-risk action the farmer can take now.
Give one action that reduces accidental spread.
Recommend local expert confirmation before treatment or removal.
template.monitoring: Explain what to watch, where to look, and when to check again.
template.seek_help: Explain which changes should prompt help from a local extension agent.
template.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

fallback.title: Guidance Unavailable
fallback.summary: This diagnosis does not yet have local guidance in the app.
actions: Keep the affected plant or field area marked so it can be checked again.
Avoid moving cuttings, seed, leaves, or tools from the affected area.
Ask a local extension agent to inspect the crop before treatment or removal.
fallback.monitoring: Take another clear photo if symptoms change or spread to nearby plants.
fallback.seek_help: Seek local help if symptoms spread quickly, plants begin dying, or food production is at risk.
fallback.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

maize_healthy.title: Healthy Maize
maize_healthy.summary: The photo is most similar to healthy maize in the classes supported by this prototype.
actions: Continue normal field care and record the date of this check.
Inspect several nearby plants instead of relying on one leaf.
Keep seed and tools clean when moving between fields.
maize_healthy.monitoring: Check again during regular field visits and photograph any new streaks, spots, rust-colored growth, or leaf drying.
maize_healthy.seek_help: Ask an extension agent for help if symptoms appear on several plants or the crop begins declining despite a healthy result.
maize_healthy.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

maize_streak_disease.title: Maize Streak Disease
maize_streak_disease.summary: The image resembles maize streak disease, which commonly appears as narrow pale or yellow streaks running along the leaf.
actions: Mark the affected plants and compare them with nearby maize.
Do not save seed from plants that are weak or heavily affected.
Ask a local extension agent to confirm the result before removing plants or applying treatment.
maize_streak_disease.monitoring: Watch for new pale streaks, stunting, and symptoms spreading to younger plants.
maize_streak_disease.seek_help: Seek help if many young plants show streaking or growth is becoming uneven across the field.
maize_streak_disease.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

maize_northern_leaf_blight.title: Northern Leaf Blight
maize_northern_leaf_blight.summary: The image resembles northern leaf blight, often associated with long gray-green or tan lesions on maize leaves.
actions: Mark affected areas and inspect leaves at different heights on nearby plants.
Avoid carrying wet infected leaves or residue into unaffected fields.
Discuss locally suitable resistant varieties and field practices with an extension agent.
maize_northern_leaf_blight.monitoring: Check whether lesions are increasing after humid or rainy conditions and whether upper leaves become affected.
maize_northern_leaf_blight.seek_help: Seek help if lesions reach the upper canopy, spread rapidly, or appear before flowering.
maize_northern_leaf_blight.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

maize_common_rust.title: Common Rust
maize_common_rust.summary: The image resembles common rust, which can form small raised orange-brown or dark pustules on maize leaves.
actions: Inspect both sides of several leaves for raised rust-colored spots.
Keep a record of where symptoms are concentrated in the field.
Ask an extension agent whether local varieties or management changes are recommended.
maize_common_rust.monitoring: Watch whether pustules increase on younger leaves or begin covering large leaf areas.
maize_common_rust.seek_help: Seek help if rust becomes widespread early in crop growth or leaves begin drying quickly.
maize_common_rust.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

maize_unknown.title: Unknown Maize Condition
maize_unknown.summary: The photo appears to show maize, but it does not reliably match the healthy or maize disease classes supported by this model.
actions: Take additional photos of the whole plant and both sides of affected leaves.
Do not apply treatment based only on this result.
Keep affected plant material separate until a local expert can inspect it.
maize_unknown.monitoring: Record changes in color, leaf shape, spots, streaks, insect damage, and the number of affected plants.
maize_unknown.seek_help: Ask an extension agent to inspect the crop if symptoms persist, spread, or reduce plant growth.
maize_unknown.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

cassava_healthy.title: Healthy Cassava
cassava_healthy.summary: The photo is most similar to healthy cassava in the classes supported by this prototype.
actions: Continue normal field care and record the date of this check.
Inspect several nearby plants and both young and older leaves.
Use clean tools and healthy-looking planting material for future cuttings.
cassava_healthy.monitoring: Check again during regular visits and photograph new mosaic patterns, brown streaks, wilting, angular spots, or stem damage.
cassava_healthy.seek_help: Ask an extension agent for help if several plants decline even though this photo was classified as healthy.
cassava_healthy.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

cassava_brown_streak_disease.title: Cassava Brown Streak Disease
cassava_brown_streak_disease.summary: The image resembles cassava brown streak disease, which may involve yellow or brown leaf patterns, stem streaks, and root damage.
actions: Mark the affected plants and do not distribute cuttings from them.
Inspect nearby cassava for similar leaf or stem symptoms.
Ask an extension agent to confirm the result and advise on clean planting material.
cassava_brown_streak_disease.monitoring: Watch for increasing leaf discoloration, brown stem streaks, and symptoms appearing in neighboring plants.
cassava_brown_streak_disease.seek_help: Seek help promptly if symptoms are widespread or harvested roots show brown, cork-like damage.
cassava_brown_streak_disease.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

cassava_bacterial_blight.title: Cassava Bacterial Blight
cassava_bacterial_blight.summary: The image resembles cassava bacterial blight, which may cause angular leaf spots, wilting, leaf drop, or stem dieback.
actions: Avoid handling affected plants when leaves are wet.
Clean tools before using them on healthy cassava and do not share affected cuttings.
Ask an extension agent to confirm the cause before removing plants.
cassava_bacterial_blight.monitoring: Watch for water-soaked or angular spots, wilting shoots, sticky stem exudate, and spread after rain.
cassava_bacterial_blight.seek_help: Seek help if shoots die back, many plants wilt, or symptoms spread rapidly after wet weather.
cassava_bacterial_blight.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

cassava_mosaic_disease.title: Cassava Mosaic Disease
cassava_mosaic_disease.summary: The image resembles cassava mosaic disease, commonly associated with patchy green and yellow leaf patterns and distorted leaves.
actions: Mark the affected plant and do not use or distribute cuttings from it.
Inspect nearby cassava, especially young leaves, for similar mosaic patterns.
Ask a local extension agent to confirm the result before removal or replanting.
cassava_mosaic_disease.monitoring: Watch for stronger mosaic patterns, twisted leaves, stunting, and symptoms appearing on neighboring plants.
cassava_mosaic_disease.seek_help: Seek help if many plants are affected, young plants are stunted, or clean planting material is difficult to find.
cassava_mosaic_disease.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

cassava_unknown.title: Unknown Cassava Condition
cassava_unknown.summary: The photo appears to show cassava, but it does not reliably match the healthy or cassava disease classes supported by this model.
actions: Take additional photos of the whole plant, stem, and both sides of affected leaves.
Do not distribute cuttings or apply treatment based only on this result.
Keep the plant marked for inspection by a local extension agent.
cassava_unknown.monitoring: Record changes in leaf color, shape, wilting, stem damage, insects, and the number of affected plants.
cassava_unknown.seek_help: Ask an extension agent to inspect the crop if symptoms persist, spread, or affect roots and stems.
cassava_unknown.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

rice_healthy.title: Healthy Rice
rice_healthy.summary: The photo is most similar to healthy rice in the classes supported by this prototype.
actions: Continue normal field care and record the date of this check.
Inspect rice in several parts of the field rather than relying on one leaf.
Clean tools and footwear before moving between fields.
rice_healthy.monitoring: Check again during regular visits and photograph new lesions, yellowing, drying leaf tips, or panicle damage.
rice_healthy.seek_help: Ask an extension agent for help if symptoms appear across the field despite this healthy result.
rice_healthy.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.title: Bacterial Leaf Blight
rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.summary: The image resembles bacterial leaf blight, which may cause water-soaked streaks, yellowing, and drying from leaf tips or edges.
actions: Mark affected field areas and avoid moving contaminated plant material or tools.
Avoid unnecessary leaf injury and discuss locally appropriate water and nutrient management.
Ask an extension agent to confirm the result before treatment.
rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.monitoring: Watch for lesions extending down the leaf, rapid yellowing, wilting seedlings, or spread after storms.
rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.seek_help: Seek help if young plants wilt, lesions spread rapidly, or large field areas begin drying.
rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

rice_blast.title: Rice Blast
rice_blast.summary: The image resembles rice blast, often associated with spindle-shaped leaf lesions and possible damage at nodes or panicle necks.
actions: Inspect nearby leaves, nodes, and panicle necks for related lesions.
Avoid moving affected straw or seed into unaffected fields.
Ask an extension agent about locally suitable varieties and nutrient management.
rice_blast.monitoring: Watch for new spindle-shaped lesions, broken nodes, or panicles that whiten and fail to fill.
rice_blast.seek_help: Seek help quickly if symptoms reach panicle necks, spread during humid weather, or threaten grain filling.
rice_blast.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

rice_yellow_mottle_disease.title: Rice Yellow Mottle Disease
rice_yellow_mottle_disease.summary: The image resembles rice yellow mottle disease, which may cause yellow or mottled leaves, stunting, and poor panicle development.
actions: Mark affected patches and avoid moving plants, tools, or water from them into unaffected areas.
Clean tools and footwear after working in affected field sections.
Ask an extension agent to confirm the result and advise on locally appropriate resistant varieties.
rice_yellow_mottle_disease.monitoring: Watch for expanding yellow patches, stunting, delayed flowering, and poor panicle emergence.
rice_yellow_mottle_disease.seek_help: Seek help if symptoms spread between field patches or many plants become stunted.
rice_yellow_mottle_disease.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.

rice_unknown.title: Unknown Rice Condition
rice_unknown.summary: The photo appears to show rice, but it does not reliably match the healthy or rice disease classes supported by this model.
actions: Take additional photos of the whole plant, leaf surfaces, stem base, and panicle if present.
Do not apply treatment based only on this result.
Keep affected field areas marked until a local extension agent can inspect them.
rice_unknown.monitoring: Record changes in lesions, yellowing, wilting, insect damage, plant height, and panicle development.
rice_unknown.seek_help: Ask an extension agent to inspect the crop if symptoms persist, spread, or begin reducing plant growth or grain formation.
rice_unknown.disclaimer: Prototype guidance only. This result is not a confirmed diagnosis.
